releases.title: collectZ v3.25.2
releases.summary: Remediates reported vulnerabilities in CollectZ's development and build tooling. Vite and its source-map dependency are upgraded to fixed releases, and the backend development command now uses Node's built-in watch mode instead of Nodemon and its affected watcher tree.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Upgrade frontend Vite from affected `8.0.16` to `8.3.5` and lock `source-map-js` to `1.2.2`, addressing the reported Vite/launch-editor and source-map-js advisories.

Replace `nodemon server.js` with `node --watch server.js` and remove Nodemon from backend development dependencies. This removes the backend watcher chain that included vulnerable `braces` and `brace-expansion` packages.
Keep backend and frontend production dependencies on the previously patched `follow-redirects@1.16.1`.
Synchronize app metadata and Help > Releases to `3.25.2`.

releases.title: collectZ v3.25.1
releases.summary: Moves CollectZ's Node 24 runtime, build, CI, and operational helper environments to Node `24.22.1`, the security-fixed Node 24 maintenance-LTS release. The previous canonical backend container was running Node `24.21.0`, which predates the October 21 security release.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Pin backend and frontend build images, syslog and sizing helper images, and the local dependency-audit image to `node:24.22.1-alpine`.
Pin active Node-based GitHub Actions workflows to Node `24.22.1` and add `.nvmrc` for maintainers.
Raise the declared minimum backend engine to `>=24.22.1 <25` and add source-contract coverage for all maintained runtime and CI selectors.
Update the backend and frontend `follow-redirects` override from `1.16.0` to `1.16.1` to resolve two newly reported high-severity advisories found during release preflight.
Document that `npm audit` covers package dependencies, not the Node runtime and its bundled OpenSSL, c-ares, CA certificates, and Undici components.

releases.title: collectZ v3.25.0
releases.summary: Adds a native Apple TV companion for CollectZ with browser-approved sign-in, read-only collection browsing, and the existing CollectZ visual identity. The SwiftUI client is maintained in the sibling `collectZ-tvos` repository.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: TV pairing and browsing work in both deployment modes, including installations with Cairn. Every read still requires current library/workspace membership; archived workspaces are excluded.
Native screens use only the CollectZ name. Debug simulator builds recognize bare localhost and private IPv4 LAN addresses as HTTP; public connections and Release builds still require HTTPS.
Browser `/activate` approval uses short-lived device codes, existing cookie authentication, and CSRF protection. Device credentials/codes are hashed; polling is limited and redemption is atomic.
Dedicated TV permissions reuse mobile access/refresh sessions. Existing scanner permissions are unchanged. TV sessions cannot edit data, trigger imports, or use capture APIs.
Explicit library selection checks current membership on every read, including administrator accounts, without changing the web application's active library.
TV responses expose safe metadata and authorized artwork paths rather than raw integration payloads or source URLs. Collection joins check linked media ownership.
Native tvOS 18+ screens use CollectZ's colors, logo, bundled fonts, cards, and badges, with remote focus, accessible labels, stale states, and Keychain credentials.
Updated compatible axios and proxy-addr lockfile resolutions to remove production dependency advisories identified during release validation.

releases.title: collectZ v3.24.14
releases.status: complete locally against PostgreSQL 16; canonical Docker stack and hosted release gates pending
releases.summary: The backend no longer runs as the PostgreSQL owner/superuser. A one-shot `migrate` service applies migrations and provisions a least-privilege `collectz_app` role with the owner credential, then exits. The backend connects only as that role, and it refuses to start if its database credential is a superuser, owns application tables, or could bypass future row-level security.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Added a one-shot `migrate` Compose service built from the backend image. It runs `scripts/migrate-and-provision.js`, which applies pending migrations, creates or updates the runtime role, then connects as that role to verify it before exiting. The backend waits for it to complete successfully.

The runtime role is created with `NOSUPERUSER`, `NOCREATEDB`, `NOCREATEROLE`, `NOREPLICATION`, and `NOBYPASSRLS`. It gets `SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE` on application tables and `USAGE/SELECT/UPDATE` on sequences. It cannot create schemas or objects, cannot truncate, index, or disable triggers, and has read-only access to `schema_migrations`. Owner default privileges give tables from future migrations the same grants.

The role password is sent to PostgreSQL as a SCRAM-SHA-256 verifier computed by the job, so the plaintext never appears in SQL text or server statement logs. Each run removes any stray role membership that would let the runtime role inherit owner rights.

Added a backend startup privilege guard (`DATABASE_RUNTIME_ROLE_POLICY`, `enforce` in Compose). It fails closed on superuser, `CREATEROLE`, `CREATEDB`, `REPLICATION`, or `BYPASSRLS`; on owned or inherited table ownership; on privileged role membership; and on schema or database `CREATE`.

With `DATABASE_MIGRATIONS_MODE=external` (Compose), the backend checks that the schema is current and will not start against an un-migrated database. The legacy in-process runner remains available as `startup` mode for ad-hoc runs and logs a warning.
Added the `runtime-role-certification` CI step and evidence artifact, a local preflight gate for that evidence, and unit coverage for the role, verifier, guard, and Compose contract.

releases.title: collectZ v3.24.13
releases.status: complete locally; hosted release gates pending
releases.summary: This maintenance release restores trustworthy dependency monitoring and main-branch release validation. It repairs Node 24 clean installs, remediates known production and tooling dependency findings, preserves Dependency Watch evidence when installs fail, and keeps migration rehearsal valid when identity certification is already current.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Updated backend CSV parsing, upload handling, mail delivery, rate limiting, IP parsing, and query-string parsing dependencies to remediated releases.
Updated frontend Vitest and refreshed root tooling transitive dependencies so clean Node 24 audits cover all three lockfiles without known vulnerabilities.
Added root tooling to Dependency Watch and made the workflow run for dependency-changing pull requests.
Kept later Dependency Watch report and artifact steps running after an earlier ecosystem failure, so a broken lockfile no longer erases the diagnostic evidence.
Changed generic migration rehearsal to select the latest real upgrade boundary while leaving identity-upgrade certification anchored to its reviewed policy marker.
Restored direct commits to `main` as the default CollectZ delivery workflow; pull requests remain available when explicitly requested or operationally necessary.
Serialized same-email registration attempts so concurrent Core self-registration returns one success and one deliberate conflict instead of leaking a database uniqueness failure as an internal error.

Made the authentication abuse smoke edition-aware: Core proves invite tokens and invitation mutation routes are unavailable, while the platform contract continues to prove atomic one-time invite claims, replay rejection, and invitation rate limiting.
Restored Core workspace-owned integration readback by deriving its internal workspace scope from the active library while keeping workspace identifiers hidden from the homelab user contract.

releases.title: collectZ v3.24.12
releases.status: complete locally; hosted release gates pending
releases.summary: This release makes CollectZ credential and support-delegation operations require a recent password confirmation bound to the current opaque browser session. A reviewed operation inventory now separates harmless masked status from key/token creation, rotation, revocation, provider testing, identity changes, and delegation, with machine-checked authority and disclosure policy.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Added a rate-limited `POST /api/auth/reauthenticate` endpoint that verifies the current password and stamps only the current browser session for a configurable 15-minute window.
Existing sessions upgrade without proof and therefore fail sensitive operations closed; fresh password logins start with recent proof.
Added reusable middleware that rejects stale or non-session credentials with the stable `recent_reauthentication_required` reason before protected mutation.

Guarded personal access token and service-account key create/revoke, platform and workspace integration credential saves/tests, Plex display/webhook token operations, support-session start, and profile email change.
Kept password change protected by its equivalent current-password proof and other-session revocation; support-session end remains an unguarded safety off-ramp.

Added a 20-operation reviewed contract covering permissions, CSRF, limiter, session authentication, reauthentication, disclosure, and audit behavior. SMTP and MFA/recovery material are explicitly recorded as unavailable with mandatory future policy.
Added shared frontend password prompting and exact-operation retry for guarded profile and integration actions.
Added live PostgreSQL proof for safe status readback, stale and sibling-session non-mutation, CSRF, wrong-password, non-session, support-delegation, limiter, and audit-retention behavior.

releases.title: collectZ v3.24.11
releases.status: complete locally; hosted CI promotion gates pending after push
releases.summary: This release removes CollectZ's final plaintext invitation-token compatibility path. Fresh and upgraded databases now store only a required unique token hash, registration claims invitations only by that hash, and maintained migration evidence proves legacy upgrade and restore behavior without retaining usable credential material.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Added migration `121` to revoke legacy invitations without a usable hash, assign non-claimable retirement hashes, clear plaintext values, remove the plaintext index and column, and enforce a non-null unique hash.
Updated the fresh-install schema to create hash-only invitations from the outset.
Removed the plaintext fallback from invitation registration while retaining advisory-lock serialization and one-time conditional consumption.
Updated the aggregate invitation inventory to prove column absence and hash completeness without exposing invitation identities or token material.
Extended generic migration rehearsal evidence to capture secret-free invitation schema state before upgrade, after upgrade, and after snapshot restore.
Updated focused unit and live abuse coverage for hash-only lookup, replay, concurrency, CSRF non-mutation, and audit hygiene.

releases.title: collectZ v3.24.10
releases.status: complete locally; hosted CI promotion gates pending after push
releases.summary: This release turns CollectZ workspace ownership from scattered conventions into a reviewed, machine-checked contract. It classifies every fresh-install table and maintained Express route, records same-workspace foreign-key expectations, certifies important jobs and provider paths, centralizes stable permission keys for workspace membership management, and adds live cross-workspace authorization proof.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Added a generated and reviewed ownership snapshot covering all fresh-install database tables, maintained route declarations, stable permission keys, and selected non-request execution paths.
Table entries identify their ownership category, authoritative ownership key, rationale, and same-workspace foreign-key expectations.
Authenticated route entries record method, ownership/locality, stable read or mutation permission, scope source, CSRF policy, and session-credential requirement.
Added stable account, platform, workspace, content, member, and integration permission keys with owner/admin/member/viewer role bundles that reject unknown permissions.
Routed workspace membership-management decisions through the stable permission evaluator while retaining the existing role assignment hierarchy.

Certified durable sync jobs, Plex webhook/reconciliation/readback, capture OCR, valuation, workspace export, media search, activity audit, and provider-backed repair paths against explicit workspace sources.
Added a live PostgreSQL-backed authorization smoke for anonymous denial, read-only mutation denial, sibling-workspace read/mutation/provider denial, identifier tampering, and durable-job isolation.
Added ownership snapshot drift and live authorization certification to the maintained RBAC CI job.

releases.title: collectZ v3.24.9
releases.status: complete locally; hosted CI promotion gates pending after push
releases.summary: This release makes authentication and invitation audit details fail closed to an explicit minimal catalog. It removes account-discovery and credential-adjacent values from security audit payloads, adds focused invitation mutation throttling and CSRF proof, and inventories legacy plaintext invitation state without exposing invitation identities or token values.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Every maintained authentication, mobile-auth, invitation, membership/ownership-transfer, CSRF, support-scope, and scope-denial activity action now has an explicit detail-key and value-type schema.
Unknown detail fields are rejected before database persistence and structured-log export; uncataloged future security-sensitive actions retain no details until deliberately classified.

Security audit callers no longer submit account or membership email addresses, token-row identifiers, profile before/after values, device names, support-requester addresses, ownership-transfer labels, or free-form SMTP errors.
Generic request-outcome audit rows retain only method, query-free path, status, and duration, without response bodies or original query strings.
Workspace invitation creation and revocation have a dedicated application-layer limiter controlled by `RATE_LIMIT_INVITE_MAX`.
Concurrent claims for the same invitation token are serialized so the losing request receives the deliberate invalid-token response instead of racing into a duplicate-account error.
Live auth abuse verification covers invitation create/revoke CSRF non-mutation, invitation limiter exhaustion, persisted detail-key allowlists, and tested sensitive-value absence.
A read-only invitation-token inventory reports aggregate active plaintext, missing-hash, and historical plaintext counts without selecting invite identities or values.

releases.title: collectZ v3.24.8
releases.status: complete locally; hosted CI promotion gates pending after push
releases.summary: This release adds a production-migration certification that proves representative authentication and authorization state still behaves as declared before upgrade, after upgrade, and after snapshot restore. It complements schema parity and row-count rehearsal with password login, concurrent sessions, verified email, active workspace/library scope, memberships and roles, personal API credentials, service credentials, audit history, and secret-free evidence.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Added a runtime-generated synthetic identity fixture with two users, owner/viewer workspace and library relationships, two concurrent sessions, invitation/reset/verification lifecycle rows, audit history, a personal access token, and a service-account key.
Added a keyed, secret-free identity manifest and explicit versioned policy for session survival or revocation, active-scope preservation or clearing, and API-credential validity or revocation.

Added baseline, production-runner upgrade, and snapshot-restore HTTP certification through the real application server while preventing automatic startup migrations only inside the explicitly gated test harness.
Added migration-range selection so every migration newer than the maintained certified marker is evaluated and identity-sensitive changes cannot be hidden by a later unrelated migration.
Added CI execution and release artifact collection for identity certification alongside init parity and generic migration rehearsal.
Replaced static migration-rehearsal identity credentials and the migration-check PostgreSQL password with runtime-derived values.
Updated migration/release checklists and local preflight artifact readback for the new certification evidence.
